name: Lenko Digitigrade Street Low
description: A low-profile shoe built for the reverse-jointed digitigrade leg — the heel sits elevated on a sculpted platform that mimics natural hock positioning, with a deep toe box that tapers into a blunt, reinforced cap. Available in matte black, dusty olive, and a faded burgundy. The upper is soft synthetic canvas with reinforced stress points at the ankle joint where geneware legs apply unusual lateral force. Common on Tier 2-3 geneware adopters who got their leg mods done cheap and need shoes that actually fit without modification.
functionality: Ergonomic platform heel engineered for digitigrade gait mechanics. Reinforced lateral ankle support for non-standard joint stress.
what_it_says: You got the legs done, you're working with what you have, and you're not paying Spire prices to walk comfortably.
story_hooks: A pair found at a crime scene still has the original purchase receipt inside — from a shop that burned down six months ago.
Lenko's digitigrade lasts are rumored to be copied from a corponation patent, and a cease-and-desist might shut the brand overnight.
